statement.p: Find the critical point of the function f(x,y)=x^{2}+y^{2}+4xy-30x

Use the Second Derivative Test to determine whether the point is
test fails
a saddle point
a local minimum
a local maximum

static.solution:
f(x,y)=x^{2}+y^{2}+4xy-30x equal to zero and solve f_x(x,y)=2x+4y-30=0 f_y(x,y)=2y+4x=0 The second equation implies that y=-2x. Substituting into the first and solving for x gives: 2x - 2x - 30=0 \Rightarrow x=-5 The corresponding value of y is y=-2(-5)=10. The critical point is (-5,10).
Now we compute the Discriminant. We find the second-order partials: f_{xx}(x,y)=2 \quad f_{yy}(x,y)=2 \quad f_{xy}(x,y)=4 The discriminant is D(x,y)=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2=2\cdot 2-(4)^2=-12
Applying the Second Derivative Test we have D(-5,10)=-12 \lt 0 The Second Derivative test implies that f(-5,10) is a saddle point.
